value.question: Can a linear probe read Lean autoformalization drift from generator activations, and does synthetic-drift training transfer to human-audited natural misformalizations?
value.hypothesis: Generators encode drift they cannot verbalize: a linear probe predicts trace correctness at 0.953, so Lean misformalizations should be linearly readable.

compute_axis.quantity: statement-runs (forward passes whose activations are cached and probed)

held_fixed: probe architecture: logistic regression C=0.1 on last-token hidden state, StandardScaler, 5-fold CV layer selection
held-out labels: 200 human-audited natural drift pairs; training labels: synthetic CPG drift
generation: greedy, bf16, max 300 new tokens per statement

predictions.if_lever: Synthetic-drift probes transfer to natural Lean misformalizations: parallel GPUs reach AUROC ≥ 0.80 at 5,000 statement-runs, sooner than one sequential GPU.
predictions.if_not: Drift is weakly readable in Lean: probe AUROC on natural misformalizations stays near 0.679 even at 150,000 statement-runs, so it never crosses the flagging threshold.
predictions.decision_rule: Held-out AUROC on the 200 human-audited natural drift pairs: ≥ 0.80 ⇒ if_lever; ≤ 0.70 ⇒ if_not; between 0.70 and 0.80 ⇒ audit 100 more statements and re-test.
predictions.noise_rule: Bootstrap 95% CI (2,000 resamples) over held-out statements; 5 probe seeds × 3 generation seeds; a real difference is one whose CI does not overlap the 0.70/0.80 thresholds.
predictions.expected_why: Synthetic probes transferred to real PII (Goodfire) and BPF catches 89.6% of Lean drift, but MATH-to-ARC transfer is only 0.54, so Lean readability is genuinely open.

value.compute_tested_why: Probe AUROC and synthetic-to-natural transfer both depend on how many statement-runs are cached; each forward pass is independent and parallelizes across GPUs, so more parallel compute buys more runs in the same wall-clock.
value.scored_against: Probe AUROC on 200 human-audited natural drift pairs, compared to the SMT-LIB priors 0.960 (solver oracle) and 0.679 (LLM-proxy intent); ≥ 0.80 counts as readable, ≤ 0.70 as not.

arms.what: logistic probe trained on synthetic CPG drift (faithful vs drifted)
logistic probe trained on the 200 human-audited natural pairs
probe trained on synthetic + natural combined

baseline.what: SMT-LIB autoformalization probe: 0.960 AUROC vs solver oracle, 0.679 vs LLM-proxy intent labels

anchor.what: Planted synthetic-drift probe hits AUROC ≥ 0.90; 4-shard parallel caching matches single-GPU sequential caching within ±0.05 AUROC; shuffle control 0.50.
anchor.independent_code: sklearn LogisticRegression (C=0.1, StandardScaler) on last-token hidden state at CV-selected layer, cross-checked with a RandomForest head.

checks: Planted synthetic-drift signal recovered at AUROC ≥ 0.90; shuffled-label control must be 0.50.
Reproduce the MATH recipe: logistic regression C=0.1, StandardScaler, 5-fold CV layer selection.
Verbalized confidence ≤ 0.70 and TF-IDF surface classifier ≤ 0.65 on the same held-out set.
4-shard parallel caching reproduces the single-GPU sequential probe within ±0.05 AUROC.

phases.what: Load DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5-RL on 1×A6000; run planted-signal and shuffle controls; measure real 7B tokens/s.
phases.stop_rule: Time box 2 hours; end when planted AUROC ≥ 0.90 and 7B throughput logged.

gate.else: stop — pipeline cannot recover an injected signal.

phases.what: Human expert labels 200 natural autoformalizer outputs faithful vs drifted.
Generate 2,000 synthetic CPG drift pairs, cache activations, train probe on synthetic, evaluate on the 200 audited pairs.

gate.else: fall back — train probes only on the 200 human labels and skip the 100k synthetic scale-up.

phases.what: Cache 100k statement-runs on 4×A6000 across six subfields, fit probes, held-out eval; then 20k-run transfers to 14B and 32B.
phases.stop_rule: End at 140k runs cached or 30 wall-hours, whichever first; shrink statement count if measured 7B throughput < 20 tok/s.

phases.what: Write AUROC vs priors, concealment gap, subfield and scale transfer table.

numbers.name: SMT-LIB SAE probe AUROC vs solver oracle

numbers.name: MATH to ARC cross-domain transfer AUROC
numbers.quote: Cross-domain transfer (MATH-trained probe applied to ARC) is weaker (0.54–0.55)

numbers.name: MATH probe held-out problems
numbers.quote: Eval: held-out AUROC on 200 separate problems

numbers.name: miniF2F Lean theorem pairs
numbers.quote: The miniF2F benchmark currently targets Metamath, Lean, Isabelle (partially) and HOL Light (partially) and consists of 488 problem statements drawn from the AIME, AMC, and the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO)

numbers.name: primary generator size
numbers.quote: We release the DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5 with 7B parameters, including base, SFT and RL models, to the public.

numbers.name: 7B generation throughput
numbers.rests_on: 7B bf16 greedy decoding on an A6000-class GPU typically runs 30–60 tokens/s.

numbers.name: 14B generation throughput
numbers.rests_on: roughly linear slowdown with parameter count versus the 7B figure.

numbers.name: 32B generation throughput
numbers.rests_on: roughly half the 7B figure on the same-class GPU.

numbers.name: 72B generation throughput
numbers.rests_on: 72B bf16 spans 2×H100 and decodes much slower than 7B.

numbers.name: planted-signal probe AUROC
numbers.rests_on: the drift signal is injected by us, so a working pipeline should nearly perfectly separate it.

numbers.name: synthetic-to-natural transfer AUROC
numbers.rests_on: Goodfire synthetic SAE probes transferred to real data, but MATH-to-ARC transfer is only 0.54; Lean synthetic drift is more controlled than cross-domain.

lines.what: Generate 2,000 synthetic CPG drift pairs and cache activations

lines.condition: Run only if core lines total under $600.

lines.what: Cached hidden states + raw text on filesystem

scenarios.what: Throughput halves; scale and transfer lines double in hours; 72B run dropped.

full_scale.what: Nine models 1.5B–72B × six subfields × 50k statement-runs (the published 9-model scale)

outside_budget.what: Expert audit of 200 natural drift pairs

restructuring.sequential_part: Expert-labelled faithful/drifted pairs, one forward pass per statement, probe fit, held-out evaluation — four steps.
restructuring.method: Synthetic drift is generated in parallel by counterfactual perturbation, and forward passes over many statements run side-by-side on separate GPUs.
restructuring.condition: Synthetic-drift-trained probes must transfer to natural misformalizations; cheap check is probe AUROC on the 200 human-audited pairs (threshold 0.70).
restructuring.baseline_sequential: One A6000 GPU running statements one at a time (greedy bf16 decoding), tuned to peak single-GPU throughput.
restructuring.baseline_copies: Four independent A6000 copies, each caching a disjoint shard of statements side by side.

scope_gap: Causal repair of drift — the MATH signal is diagnostic, not causal, so the probe only detects.
Cross-domain transfer beyond Lean — MATH-to-ARC transfer was only 0.54.
Closed autoformalizers whose weights cannot be probed.

novelty.closest_prior: A linear SAE probe reached 0.960 AUROC against an SMT-LIB solver oracle but 0.679 against intent labels; largest compute: 950 encodings, one 27B verifier.
novelty.left_open: No one has measured drift readability in Lean (only SMT-LIB), scored a probe against human audit labels, or tested synthetic-to-natural drift transfer.

limits: Shows readability, not a causal fix, and only within Lean.
Cannot prove synthetic-to-natural transfer beyond the audited 200 pairs.
value.test_summary: Cache a 7B Lean autoformalizer's hidden states over 100k+ runs; train logistic probes on synthetic drift, test on 200 human-audited natural misformalizations; time parallel 4-GPU vs sequential and sharded-copy baselines; compare AUROC to SMT-LIB 0.960/0.679.
